newsitem.title: UK: Moscow's 3-year dollar bond due next week - bankers.
newsitem.headline: Moscow's 3-year dollar bond due next week - bankers.

text.p: The City of Moscow is expected to launch its first international bond next week following an extensive global roadshow, bankers said on Thursday.
"Moscow is likely to launch its Eurobond next Tuesday after the (British) bank holiday on Monday," an emerging market syndicate official said.
Moscow is expected to launch a three-year Eurobond of between $300-$400 million.
Price talk is for a range between 300-350 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes.
"There is talk of a spread of 325-335 basis points (over U.S. Treasury notes),"a dealer said, "But this is cheap."
Credit Suisse First Boston and Nomura will be joint lead managers for Moscow's transaction.
Bankers said they had heard there was "incredible demand" for the deal from the U.S. and Europe.

Last week Moscow's chairman of the committee for municipal loans & stock market Mechislav Klimovich said Moscow would consider launching a second Eurobond this year if its upcoming Eurobond was well-received.
Klimovich said Moscow was limited to raise $500 million this year.
Moscow is rated Ba2 by Moody's Investors Service and BB- by Standard & Poor's.
Klimovich also said that the city's ratings were constrained by the sovereign ceiling.
